prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators in spin-orbit-coupled, time-reversal-invariant materials, and the experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B047 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp as a single prize part. Kane and Mele showed that time-reversal-invariant insulators with spin-orbit coupling fall into two classes labelled by a Z2 invariant, a result that can be computed from a band structure and that predicts counter-propagating edge channels. Molenkamp's group then measured the conductance of HgTe wells and found the protected edge transport, so the prize would reward a prediction that was tested. The interpretation has been stable for fifteen years or more across many materials. Round 1 sharpened the one question that matters most, which is the 2016 overlap, and I now think it has an answer that can go into the citation. The 2016 prize recognised the Thouless-Kosterlitz transition and the Haldane and TKNN line, in which the invariant is an integer Chern number tied to broken time-reversal symmetry and a quantised Hall conductance. The Z2 insulator needs no magnetic field or broken symmetry, has no net charge Hall current, and depends on spin-orbit coupling and time-reversal symmetry. That is a different classification and a different measurable signature, not a late second helping of the same discovery.
statement.case_against: Three weaknesses remain and none is resolved. First, the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal that told Molenkamp which material to grow is not in the credited names, and Zhang cannot be recognised, so the experimental half rests on one name whose measurement followed another group's design; the citation can say 'HgTe quantum wells' but cannot give that credit in the names. Second, Hasan's three-dimensional observation, with Fu, Moore and others, is left out and a later part cannot be assumed. Third, the 2016 distinction I draw above is my own argument, and a colleague who weighs the Haldane model as the real origin of topological insulators could reasonably reject it. I also accept that B010 has the cleanest two-name attribution on the shortlist, so on credit alone B047 is weaker than B010.

responses.point: Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce prefer B010 for Katori and Ye, citing the cleanest credit boundary, independent reproduction near 1e-18, and a citation framed on the magic-wavelength lattice to separate it from the 2005 and 2012 prizes.
responses.response: I now accept that the magic-wavelength framing answers the novelty objection better than I allowed in round 1: the scheme is a distinct invention from the comb and from ion trapping. I therefore no longer call B010 incremental, and I have moved it from outside my alternatives to my first alternative. Our remaining disagreement is on weighing, not on whether B010 is a serious prize. When the achievement is better measurement of a quantity that is already defined, I put it below a result that changed how condensed-matter physicists classify phases, and I do not see that Kroll's point about timing, with the redefinition of the second still pending, outweighs this. I read the weighing question as one of judgement, and I hold my position on it.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that B010 is one of the few candidates where neither attribution nor maturity is seriously in doubt, and notes that B047 has more top-three placements while B010 has the cleaner credit.
responses.response: On attribution you are right, and I have said above that B047 is weaker on credit than B010. But the credit problem for B047 is on the margin: nobody has proposed a different core than Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. The disputed names are Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Hasan, and the committee has to decide whether a three-person limit should push us to the cleaner prize or whether a flawed but defensible allocation is acceptable. I think the second, because the credit problem is about who is left out, while the scientific case is not in doubt. I would not oppose B010 if the committee prefers clean attribution, and your point that the citation should avoid leaning on the redefinition of the second is one I share.

responses.point: Mehlig calls the recognition conceptually overdue and raises a two-part configuration pairing B047 with a precision or quantum-technology achievement.
responses.response: I qualified 'overdue' in round 1 and the Haldane distinction I give above is my answer to my own qualification. On the two-part idea: B047 plus B010 would be five names, and the protocol allows at most three unique people, so it cannot be done with the credited names. Dropping Mele or Molenkamp to make room would break the theory-and-experiment link, which is the reason I support the prize. I therefore keep a single part and do not support a two-part split here.

responses.point: Johansson supports the Kane, Mele and Molenkamp trio, wonders whether Hasan's 3D work is better treated in a later year, and names B046 as a cleaner configuration if the allocation cannot be settled.
responses.response: I agree that the 3D work is best treated as a separate later achievement: the strong topological insulator in Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 was a new materials discovery with a different experimental probe, whereas the Z2 invariant and HgTe edge channels form a complete chain on their own. For the same reason I would keep Mele over Hasan, which differs from Danielsson's proposal. Where I part from you is on B046 as a fall-back: it has no first-place ranking, three ranked placements, and Cirac and Zoller are not tied to a single experiment in the way Kane, Mele and Molenkamp are, so I do not see it as a cleaner configuration for me.

responses.point: Danielsson would honour the observed correlated and superconducting states in B051 without asserting a pairing mechanism, and would put Hasan in place of Mele in B047 or would not oppose B047 if attribution is settled.
responses.response: I take the citation proposal seriously and it would be a defensible wording, but it does not change my view on timing. Earlier prizes did honour observed phenomena before a full explanation, and I accept that. In B051, however, the origin of the correlated insulators and the superconductivity is the thing the experiment discovered, and with the mechanism open, the physical content that the citation would credit is thin. I keep B051 as a second alternative. On Mele versus Hasan, the Kane-Mele paper is the origin of the Z2 invariant and the HgTe experiment tests that prediction, so I keep Mele, and I count your willingness not to oppose B047 as helpful.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts the argument that the time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulator is distinct from the Chern-insulator and Haldane line recognised in 2016, or reads B047 as a continuation
Whether a prize that names only Molenkamp for the experiment, and not Bernevig, Hughes or Zhang for the proposal, or Hasan for the 3D observation, is acceptable under the three-person limit

Whether weighing a new classification of phases above a precision-measurement invention is a scientific judgement the committee shares, since I have no independent way to settle it and the four B010 supporters weigh credit boundary and confirmed performance more heavily
My statements on priority history, including who proposed HgTe and the roles of Fu, Moore and Hasan, come from recollection and not from verified documentation
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged. My field (electronic-structure theory, DFT, DMFT and magnetism) is close to the band-theory side of B047 and to B018, which I ranked first in the opening ballot; B018 is not part of my final position and I am not advocating it. My profile lists no personal or institutional connection to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer. I see no conflict that requires recusal.
